# Halloween: spider webs

Select `CobwebLoop` in the Studio. The preset `presets/halloween-cobweb.json` creates a **12-second, 1920×1080, 60 fps** loop in MP4/WebM, with the webs gathered in the four corners — the largest one at the top right corner, under the moon — and the middle of the frame free of large elements; only the dust crosses the whole frame, at low brightness, and the mist runs close to the ground, below the central area. The composition's own initial values are `seed: 47`, `backgroundColor: #100B1B` and the palette below. There is no text, external images, extra fonts or audio.

Each web is made of radial threads and thin capture rings, in arcs that sag towards the web's hub, anchored in the corner, and hang a little under their own weight; the stronger outer ring closes the outline. The seed sets where the tear falls, always in view, with broken ends each hanging from a knot, and the small irregularities; only the two top webs have a broken strand, with a drop at its tip. Neither that strand nor the ends of the tear hang next to a spider's line, even with `spiderCount: 3`. Each web's drawing does not change during the cycle; the breeze only bends it. The spokes always end at the outer ring, which is never torn, so no spoke has its tip loose in the air.

A single breeze crosses the frame from left to right each cycle — a gust, a weaker puff and then calm: the webs, held by the hub and by the spokes on both edges, billow with the wind, first the ones on the left and then the ones on the right, carrying along the dew, the ends of the tear and the broken strand; the same gust tilts the silk strands, pushes nearby dust more than distant dust and increases the spiders' swing. With the hub held in the corner, the webs also sway and breathe slowly, out of step with each other, and each one breathes with its own amplitude. A band of moonlight travels across each web's silk, from one side of the fan to the other, and the dew drops glint one by one as it passes, keeping a discreet shine between passes. The silk strands hang from fixed knots above the top edge, well spaced from each other and from each spider's line, and swing at the tip, with a drop at the end. They are longer on the sides and shorter over the center, except in the column of each of the three possible spiders, even those `spiderCount` hides: there they are short enough to end above the spider's legs, which is why the strands near the right edge are the shortest, whatever `spiderCount` is. The dust rises slowly at different depths — the nearest is larger and wanders more — and vanishes before starting again at the bottom. Each spider repeats the same scene on its own thread, swinging like a pendulum: it rests at the top, lets go, is caught by the line while still falling and bounces on it until it stops, rests at the bottom and climbs back up in four pulls. At rest, the legs barely move; while the spider falls or climbs, they move as if it were walking. With `spiderCount: 3`, the three spiders take turns and never fall together.

The light comes from a moon close to the top edge, near the top right corner: the main web shows backlit against the halo; on each web, the spokes, the rings and the broken strand get a light edge shifted towards the side where the moon is, seen from the corner where the web is anchored, with the shadow on the opposite side; the hanging silk strands have the light edge on the moon's side and the shadow on the other; and the drops are glass beads with the reflection turned towards it. The spider is a dark silhouette with jointed legs, a waist, palps and an amber hourglass; a thread of moonlight outlines the body and the legs on the moon's side. An amber ember below the bottom edge lights the bottom left web from below. `colors[0]` controls the silk, the mist and the diffuse sky glow around the moon, `colors[1]` the moon's halo, the moonlight that falls on the silk and the spider, the glints and the dew, and `colors[2]` the amber warmth of the low light, of the warm reflection on the bottom left web, of the dust and drops near that light and of the spider's mark; the core of the drops and the dust follows `colors[1]`, with a white highlight on each drop. The dust shows where the light reaches it: bright under the moon, amber over the ember and fainter in the dark corners. With only two colors, the amber takes the first. The seed sets the webs' geometry, the loose strands, the dust and the dew's twinkle; the breeze, the mist and the spiders follow the same path with any seed. `webCount` picks how many corners get a web, in the order top right (the main web, under the moon), bottom left, top left and bottom right; `webCount: 0` removes the webs and, with them, the dew. `strandCount: 0`, `moteCount: 0` and `spiderCount: 0` hide those layers; `dewIntensity: 0` turns off the dew and `mistIntensity: 0` removes the mist. Changing the count of one layer does not rearrange the others.

With `transparent: true` and `outputFormat: "webm"`, the sky, the vignette and the diffuse glow around the moon disappear, keeping webs, dew, strands, spiders, dust and mist with alpha. As background light, only the moon's halo, at the top right corner, and an amber band at the bottom edge remain, both outside the central area; the moonlight and the amber reflection on the silk stay, and a discreet dark outline under the silk keeps the threads legible over bright video. The spider has an opaque body, the moonlight edge of the legs keeps it visible over dark video, and the thread holding it has a discreet shadow so it does not vanish over bright video. In MP4/GIF, every element is composited over `backgroundColor`.

## Overlay kit

The [`halloween-cobweb`](../overlays.md#themes) theme dresses chat, blocks and borders for this background, with the same 12 s and seed 47: `presets/chat-halloween-cobweb.json`, `presets/block-halloween-cobweb.json` and `presets/border-halloween-cobweb.json`, and the pack comes out with `npm run render:pack -- halloween-cobweb`. The `cobweb` ornaments draw the background's webs, with the same threads, the tear and the broken ends, in the corners of the boxes, the dew glinting as the moonlight band passes and the black widow, hanging from its thread beside the chat and the blocks and resting on the web on the borders. Along the top edge hang garlands of strands, tied to fixed knots, with dew drops at the lowest points and a few broken ends; on rectangular window borders and rectangular blocks (except the labels and the Twitch panel, which has no garlands), another garland tied to the frame itself along the bottom edge. Amber only shows on the spider's hourglass and on the ember behind the bottom web. The ornaments live in the bleed, so leave about 48 px free around the webcams (72 px on `webcam-16x9-lg` and 96 px on `gameplay`, where the ornaments are enlarged) and 32 px around the chat and the blocks, including up to the screen edge and between one piece and the next: webs, garlands and the spider sit in those margins. See also [Halloween kits](../kits-halloween.md).
